title: Nobody Sees It Happen
logline: In a mid-country garden of mixed shade trees, ripe pods are cut, held a few days, broken open, and the wet seed heaped under leaves in a closed box for six days in a fixed order that cannot be paused, reordered or run again, at the end of which the seed is dead, a different substance, and past any correction — and the whole of the change that matters happens inside each bean, in the dark, where nobody watching can see it.
human_question: If the only change that counts happens where you cannot look, what is it that you are actually judging by?

place.what_kind_of_place: Mid-country garden land on the intermediate slope between the coastal lowland and the hills: steep small valleys, streams in every fold, and holdings of an acre or two planted as layered gardens rather than as fields, with a canopy of tall shade trees over an understorey of small crooked trees carrying pods straight off their trunks and main branches, and pepper, clove, nutmeg, banana and jak mixed through it. The working equipment is small and almost entirely domestic. A knife on a pole for the high pods, a basket, a heap of pods in the leaf litter, a short wooden mallet or the blunt back of a knife for breaking them, a wooden box a metre or so square with gaps in the floor, a stack of cut banana leaves, sacks, and a raised drying floor or a run of trays on trestles in the open. The instruments are a hand pushed down into the middle of the heap to feel how hot it has got, the smell coming off the box when the leaves are lifted, the liquid running out through the floor of the box and under it, and a thumbnail or a small blade run through one bean lengthwise to see how far into the middle the colour has gone. Nothing is powered and nothing is measured. The box has no lid that locks, but once it is filled and covered the six days are not interruptible in any way that would help.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because it is one of the few working processes anywhere whose decisive event is both completely ordinary and completely invisible, and because the place itself is beautiful before any of that is explained. Wide and high, a layered mid-country garden is one of the densest and most legible things in the island: a canopy in four or five storeys, mist sitting in the folds at first light, streams, and a few roofs under it, with the pods themselves showing as scattered points of yellow and deep red against the trunks when the camera comes low. Close, the film is a fixed sequence of small acts with long silences between them: a pod cut and caught, a heap of pods left lying for days doing nothing anybody can see, the pod split and the wet seed lifted out in a white sheath, the box filled and the leaves laid over, and then four days in which the only thing to film is somebody lifting a corner of leaf, putting a hand in, and putting the leaf back. And then the moment the work turns from doing to judging: a bean cut through and read. The change the whole six days exists for takes place inside the seed. It cannot be seen while it is happening, it cannot be seen afterwards except by destroying a sample of the thing you were making, and when it is over the seed is dead and nothing later in the chain — no washing, no drying, no roasting, no grinding — will put any of it back.
place.what_moves_or_changes: Everything, in one direction, on a clock nobody set. The first act happened before the film starts: the pods were cut at a ripeness judged by colour and sound, because a pod cut too early will not ferment at all and a pod left too long begins to sprout inside its own shell, and they have been lying in a heap since, which is itself a stage. Once the seed is out of the pod it is already changing, and once the box is filled and covered there is no way of opening it that improves anything. For the first two days the heap works closed and wet, the sheath around each seed breaks down and runs away through the floor of the box, and the temperature climbs. Then the whole heap is turned once, and fresh leaves are laid on, and it is turned again two days later, and the air that reaches it changes what is happening inside it. Somewhere in the middle of the six days the germ in each seed dies, which is the event the entire process is for, and nobody can say to the hour when it happened. From the fifth day a bean can be cut and read. At the end the leaves come off, the beans come out hot and brown instead of white, and they go out into the sun on trays for the better part of a week, turned by hand or foot. A bean that did not go far enough stays slaty and hard in the middle for the rest of its existence.
place.when_it_looks_best: The harvest rather than a month of the calendar, and inside it a dry, still stretch, because the drying is done in the open and rain on a drying floor puts a whole lot back. The garden itself wants the half hour after first light and the last half hour, when mist sits in the folds and the canopy separates into storeys, and the low pod shots want overcast, because direct sun through a broken canopy makes the yellow and red unreadable. The box wants a shed dark enough that steam reads when the leaves come off, and the drying floor wants the hard middle of the day, which is when it is actually worked. The six days of the ferment have to be filmed as six days and not as a montage, because the film's whole argument is that four of them look like nothing.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about one lot of seed, followed from the tree to the sacks. A layered garden at first light with mist in the folds; a knife on a pole and pods dropping into leaf litter; a heap of pods lying in the shade for several days with nothing happening; pods broken and the wet white seed lifted out by the handful; a box filled, banana leaves laid over, and then four days in which the only events are a hand going into the heap and a corner of leaf being put back; liquid running out under the box; the turn, and fresh leaves; the lid off and the heap steaming and brown; a bean cut through and looked at; a hundred more cut and sorted into three piles; and then the sun, the trays, the raking, the sacks. It has a complete shape said out loud by nobody: a thing that has to be caught at the right ripeness, a wait that cannot be shortened, a closed run of six days that either works or does not, and a test that can only be done by destroying what you are testing. Anyone who likes layered gardens, heat, patience, or a craft whose whole difficulty is that you cannot watch it happen has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same six days become the sources' account of the one process this group exists to describe, filmed in the only honest way available, which is by showing what cannot be shown. The texts set out a fixed order of mind-moments that runs after conduct, after a settled mind, and after nine stages of seeing: preparation, access, conformity, then the single moment that first takes the unconditioned as its object, then one moment of path, then the fruit, all inside one run and none of it repeatable at the same level. Their own pictures for it are a man swinging over a canal on a rope and standing unsteady on the far bank, and an archer with his face bound in a cloth who splits a hundred planks on a signal from a stick because he cannot see the target at all. A process in which the decisive change happens inside a sealed heap, which cannot be paused or run again, which nobody can watch, and which is afterwards checked by an audit rather than celebrated, carries the shape of that without pretending to show the thing itself. The voice says plainly what it cannot show. Nothing on this screen is the unconditioned, no shot of anything is, nobody in this garden is presented as having attained anything, and the grading of beans is not a grading of people.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high over a mid-country valley. A layered garden in four or five storeys, mist standing in the folds, streams, a few roofs under the canopy. Then low and close: the small crooked trees under the shade, with pods growing straight out of the trunks, yellow and deep red against the bark.
sequence.voice: Everything this garden is about to do takes six days, and for four of those days there will be nothing to see. What the six days are for happens inside each of those pods, after they have been cut, in a closed box, in the dark. Nobody who does this work has ever watched it happen. Neither will we.

sequence.on_screen: The cut: a knife on a pole taking a ripe pod off a trunk, and the pod caught or dropped into leaf litter. A basket filling. Then a heap of pods lying in the shade, filmed twice several days apart in the same frame, with nothing visibly different between the two.
sequence.voice: The books are exact about the order and exact that none of it is a leap. One run of mind-moments, and the moments are named: preparation, access, conformity, the change of lineage, the path, and the fruit — all of them arising in a single line of impulsion [C100-P4:L42], inside a limit of seven places, with the absorption falling at the fourth or the fifth [C100-P4:L74]. A quicker person has no preparation moment; a slower person does [C100-M:L13; C100-M:L17]. It is a sequence with a floor and a ceiling, not a moment of courage.

sequence.on_screen: Pods broken with the blunt back of a knife, split open, and the wet seed lifted out in its white sheath by the handful. The box filled, the surface levelled by hand, banana leaves laid over it and pressed down. Gaps in the floor of the box, and the ground under it, dry.
sequence.voice: And the books are exact about what has to have happened before any of that order can begin. This run comes after conduct has been made clean, after the mind has been settled, and after the six worldly purifications have been completed; only then does the seventh one, the knowledge in the four paths, arise at all [C100-P:L93]. In one person's whole continuum there are four of these runs and no more, one for each path [C100-P:L25]. There is no version of this that starts here.

sequence.on_screen: Days two to five, filmed as days. Liquid running out through the floor of the box and soaking into the ground beneath. A corner of leaf lifted, a hand pushed down into the middle of the heap, the hand withdrawn, the leaf put back. The turn: the whole heap forked over and fresh leaves laid on. Steam. No dialogue at any point.
sequence.voice: There is an archer in these books, and he is the reason this film is possible. He stands eight measures off, on a turning wheel, with his face bound in a cloth, and a hundred planks are set up. A second man turns the wheel, and at the instant the planks come round he strikes a signal with a stick. The archer, not missing the signal, looses, and splits all hundred [C100-P4:L61–L67]. The signal is the moment of change of lineage; the archer is the path. He does not see what he is shooting at. Neither does the hand in this box. It is reading heat and smell, on day four, of something it cannot open.

sequence.on_screen: The leaves off. The heap brown, hot, steaming, completely unlike what went in. Then the first cut test: one bean held on a board and sliced through its length with a small blade, and the cut face held up — the colour, how far into the middle it has gone, the fissures inside.
sequence.voice: This is where the books give their own picture, and where this film says what it cannot do. A man wanting the far bank of a great canal runs, takes hold of a rope hanging from a branch, swings, arrives over the far side with his weight carrying him on, lets the rope go, and lands trembling, and only slowly stands [C100-P4:L44–L46]. That is their image and not ours, and we are not going to stage it. Their point in giving it is that the letting go and the standing are two different moments. But the thing the image is an image of cannot be filmed by anybody, because what that one moment takes as its object is the unconditioned, and there is no shot of anything that is that. A bean cut open is a bean cut open.

sequence.on_screen: A hundred beans bisected in a row on a board and sorted, without ceremony, into piles: gone all the way through, partly, and the ones still slaty and purple in the middle. A tally on a scrap of paper. Nobody pleased, nobody disappointed.
sequence.voice: What follows in the books is not a celebration. It is five reviewings, taken in order: the road that was taken, what it gave, which defilements are gone, which ones are still there, and last of all the state arrived at [C100-P4:L83–L93]. The books admit that some people leave the two middle ones out [C100-P4:L95], and that only somebody entirely finished has nothing left on the list of what remains. This is an audit. The one who has got furthest is the one best able to name exactly what has not been dealt with.

sequence.on_screen: The slaty beans among the good ones on the drying trays, going out into the sun with everything else. Raking, turning by foot, the trays pulled in against rain, days of it. The sacks at the end.
sequence.voice: The books name three ways a thing can be got rid of, and only the third one is what they mean here. It can be held down, the way ordinary concentration holds the hindrances down while it lasts [C098-P4:L209]. It can be displaced for a time by its opposite [C098-P4:L211]. Or it can be cut off, so that what could have arisen does not arise again [C098-P4:L205; C098-P4:L247]. Their own picture for the third is a young tree cut down before it has ever fruited: the fruit it has not borne is not destroyed, it simply never comes [C098-P4:L145]. And they are careful about what is removed — not past states, which have ceased, nor future ones, which do not yet exist, but the ground in which they could stand [C098-P4:L143; C098-P4:L149]. These slaty ones can be washed, dried, roasted and ground, and they will still be exactly what they are.

sequence.on_screen: Last light from height. In one frame: the garden, the shed, the empty box upside down, the drying trays stacked, the sacks. The valley going dark under mist.
sequence.voice: Three things this film is not saying. The books' noble persons are defined by what has been abandoned and by nothing else, and the path is said to last a single moment, too brief for anyone to look for [C098-M:L5; C098-M:L7]. They are not levels a person climbs to, nothing a camera sees could tell you who is one, and the books themselves say that somebody who has made this change may afterwards be very heedless indeed [C100-P4:L81]. Nobody in this garden is anything. Nobody's steadiness here is an attainment, this lot of beans is not anybody's reward, and the three piles on that board are beans.

concept_merge.why_together: C100 is the process and C098 is what the process does. C100 gives the fixed order and names its moments: preparation, access, conformity, change of lineage, path and fruit, all in one line of impulsion [C100-P4:L42], inside a seven-place limit with the absorption at the fourth or fifth [C100-P4:L74], with the preparation moment present for the slower person and absent for the quicker [C100-M:L13; C100-M:L17]. It puts the whole run downstream of everything else, since it arises only when the six worldly purifications have been completed [C100-P:L93], and it holds that there are four such runs in a person's entire continuum and no more [C100-P:L25]. It supplies both of the film's usable images: the canal and the rope, where letting go and standing firm are given to two different moments [C100-P4:L44–L46], and the blindfolded archer on the turning wheel who splits a hundred planks on a stick signal because he cannot see the target [C100-P4:L61–L67]. It supplies the reviewings, which are an audit with an honest count of what remains [C100-P4:L83–L93; C100-P4:L95]. And it supplies the flat correction that a person who has made this change may still be heedless [C100-P4:L81]. C098 supplies the kind of change involved, in terms that keep it out of the language of heroism: three ways of abandoning, of which suppression and temporary displacement are the reversible two and cutting off is the third [C098-P4:L205; C098-P4:L209; C098-P4:L211; C098-P4:L247]; the young tree cut before fruiting, where the fruit is not destroyed but simply never comes [C098-P4:L145]; the careful statement that what is removed is not past, future or present states but the ground in which they could stand [C098-P4:L143; C098-P4:L149]; and the definition of the noble persons by what has been abandoned, with the path lasting a single moment too brief to be looked for [C098-M:L5; C098-M:L7]. A six-day closed ferment in which the decisive event happens inside a seed, in the dark, on a clock nobody set, which cannot be paused, reordered or run again on the same material, and which is afterwards checked by destroying a sample rather than by looking at the result, holds all of that without any of it being illustrated.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the hardest thing in this group is not the size of the change but the fact that it cannot be watched, and that the honest way to film it is to film a process with the same property and then say out loud what the footage does not contain. Stated flat, C100 is a list of mind-moments that a reader will immediately convert into an epiphany, which is precisely what its digest forbids. Put on a six-day ferment it becomes three unfamiliar and correct things at once: it is long rather than instantaneous at the level of preparation, it is over before anybody notices at the level of the event, and it is invisible throughout. The pairing with C098 supplies the irreversibility without any drama: the change is not that something was overcome but that a ground was removed, and the source's own image for it is a tree that simply never fruits. The film's reviewing beat is the part that would be impossible anywhere else, because a cut test is literally a count of how far the change went and how much did not go, performed by cutting open the thing you have made, and the sources' five reviewings end on the honest total of what remains. This idea has been round once before and has been rebuilt from the ground. Its previous version filmed people crossing a stream by a rope tied to a tree, which was the sources' own canal simile taken literally. That has been dropped entirely: rope and hand-hauled crossings are a banned archetype in this slate, two other films already carry a crossing, and, more seriously, staging the simile would have delivered exactly the reading the digest names as the concept's worst — a brave moment, a threshold, a leap — with real people's daily hardship used to supply the drama. The canal image survives as a quotation, spoken once, named as the source's picture, and immediately followed by the film's statement that it is a picture of something no camera can hold.

concept_links.why: The film is this concept's order, this concept's two images and this concept's audit, and it is built so that the concept's central prohibition is structural rather than decorative. The named sequence is narrated early, with its moments in the source's order and inside its stated seven-place limit [C100-P4:L42; C100-P4:L74], and the difference between the quicker and slower person is given as the presence or absence of a preparation moment and nothing more [C100-M:L13; C100-M:L17]. The concept's placement is narrated over the box being filled: this run arises only when the six worldly purifications are complete [C100-P:L93], and there are four such runs in a whole continuum [C100-P:L25]. The archer with his face bound, who splits a hundred planks on a stick signal because he cannot see the target, is narrated over four days in which the only action is a hand going into a closed heap [C100-P4:L61–L67], and it is the image that does the film's real work, because it removes sight from the decisive act without removing preparation from it. The canal and the rope are narrated exactly once, over the first cut test, named out loud as the source's picture and not the film's, with the source's own point kept — that letting go and standing firm are two different moments — and immediately followed by the film saying that the thing the picture is a picture of cannot be filmed by anybody, because its object is the unconditioned [C100-P4:L44–L46]. The five reviewings are narrated over a hundred bisected beans being counted into three piles, in the source's own order and with its own admission that some people omit the two middle ones [C100-P4:L83–L93; C100-P4:L95]. Every limit in the digest is honoured and three of them are on screen. 'Aha moment' is refused structurally: the film contains no moment of realisation, the process it shows takes six days, the narration states that the run comes after conduct, concentration and the earlier purifications, and the digest's own wording about a fixed order is what the second beat says. 'Let go and move on' has no opening, since nothing in the film is about leaving anything behind and no simile of the cattle, the child or the burning house is used. The irreversibility is kept to this one change and is never generalised into 'no going back' about any decision, and the source's own line that a stream-enterer may be very heedless is narrated in the closing beat [C100-P4:L81]. Fruition attainment is not in the film at all, so it cannot be mistaken for a happy place or a technique; the fruition process, the signless release, the entering and emerging conditions and the deliberate time-bounding are all deliberately unused. The eight noble persons are not presented as a ladder, and 'slower' and 'quicker' are explicitly not offered as a measure of intelligence. Reviewing is not filmed or narrated as journaling or goal-tracking: it is a count, taken by destroying a sample, and its last item is not narrated as a personal achievement. The digest's unresolved items are all avoided — the reviewing arithmetic that appears to have lost a person in printing, the dry-insight tension at C100-P:L200, the two-versus-three stream-entry path names, the unclear word at C100-P4:L214, the vodāna disagreement between the sources, and the Brahma-world statement — none of which is quoted, relied on or paraphrased.

This concept gives the film the kind of change involved and the film's closing refusal. The three abandonings are narrated over the slaty beans going out into the sun with the good ones: held down by ordinary concentration while it lasts, displaced for a time by its opposite, or cut off so that what could have arisen does not arise again [C098-P4:L205; C098-P4:L209; C098-P4:L211; C098-P4:L247]. The young tree cut before it has fruited is narrated in the same beat, with the source's own emphasis that the fruit is not destroyed but simply never comes [C098-P4:L145], and the film keeps the source's careful statement that what is removed is not past states, which have ceased, nor future ones, which do not exist, but the ground in which they could stand [C098-P4:L143; C098-P4:L149]. The closing beat narrates the definition of the noble persons by what has been abandoned and the statement that the path lasts a single moment, too brief for anyone to look for [C098-M:L5; C098-M:L7]. Every limit in the digest is honoured and the sharpest of them is the closing line. 'Levels of enlightenment' as a status ladder is refused out loud: the narration says the stages are defined by what is gone and not by accomplishment, that nothing a camera sees could tell you who is one, and that nobody in the garden is anything. No real person is labelled, framed or implied to be a noble person of any stage, and no participant's steadiness or skill is presented as an attainment. 'Personal growth' has no opening, since the film's only structural claim is about a ground being removed. 'Beating your bad habits by willpower' is refused by the three-abandonings beat itself. 'An enlightened person feels nothing' cannot arise, because fruition attainment and the king's-ease comparison are not used. The chart of the ten fetters, the apportioning of greed between the paths, the forty-eight kinds of person at the third stage, the seven-lives arithmetic, the Pure Abodes and the gender-specific rebirth claim are all left out, both because the digest calls them cosmology and because the group's floor forbids any of it being turned into a statement about people on screen. Worthiness of gifts is not narrated, so nothing here justifies anybody's prosperity or comments on anybody's poverty. The two illustrative stories about elders, which the digest says are not verified facts about real places or people, are not used. The digest's flagged textual problems — the ten kilesa that print as nine, the twofold-threefold slip, the inconsistent non-returner count, the probable corruption at C098-P4:L380 and the blank once-returner column — are not quoted or relied on. And the lamp simile and the four simultaneous functions [C098-P4:L197; C098-P4:L199], which belong to this concept, are deliberately not narrated here, because the beat that could have carried them is doing the harder job of refusing the ladder, and because an image of one flame doing four things at once would pull directly against a film whose whole rhythm is six days in which four of them look like nothing.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That what these texts describe is not an epiphany but a fixed order of moments that only arises at the end of a long, ordered preparation; that its decisive instant takes as its object something no camera can show, which is why the film says so instead of showing anything; that the sources' own pictures for it are a rope over a canal, where letting go and standing firm are two different moments, and a blindfolded archer who shoots on a signal because he cannot see the target; that what such a change removes is not a past or future state but the ground a state could stand in, so that it simply does not arise again, like a tree cut before it fruits; and that what follows is an audit ending in an honest count of what is still there. The ferment is an analogy for the shape and the film says so. Nobody on screen is presented as having attained anything, the sorting of beans is not a sorting of people, and nothing here is anybody's reward or anybody's desert.
what_must_be_real: The lot's own order at its own speed, across the whole of it. The pods are not cut early for the camera, the heap is not broken sooner, the box is not filled twice, the leaves are not lifted for a shot at a time when they would not be lifted, the turn is not brought forward, and the six days are filmed as six days rather than assembled from one. If the lot comes out badly — under-fermented, over-run, rained on during drying — the film has that lot and keeps it. Nobody is asked to put a hand into the heap for the camera, to cut a test bean twice, or to explain what they are judging by. Nobody's earnings, price, buyer or debt is on screen and there is no sale in the film. No household is named or followed as a character, and nobody's patience, skill or composure is filmed, cut or narrated as a spiritual quality. The grading of beans is never intercut with people, and nothing in the edit may allow three piles on a board to stand for three kinds of person. If the garden is interplanted with a crop that this slate carries elsewhere, the film stays off it entirely: no tapping, no collection, no processing of anything but the seed this film is about.
position_hint: late in the group, and after every film that establishes order, ground and the difference between managing and ending something. It is the group's hardest film and its object is the one thing in the project that cannot be filmed, so it can only work once a viewer has already watched several processes whose order is fixed by their material. It should not be the group's last word, because it closes on an audit and a refusal rather than on anything resolved. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting the six days collapse into a moment in the edit, which would deliver the exact reading the concept's digest forbids: a breakthrough, a threshold, a brave instant.

Letting any shot stand in for the unconditioned. A beautiful still frame is not it, mist in a valley is not it, and the film has to say what it cannot show rather than reaching for an image that feels like it.
Letting the three piles of cut beans read as three grades of person, which would turn the noble persons into a ladder and the film into a sorting of human beings.
Presenting anybody's calm, patience or judgement as an attainment, which is the group's flattest prohibition and the easiest thing to do by accident with a person who works slowly.
Staging the source's canal image after quoting it, or letting a stream, a rope or a plank anywhere in the garden do the same work silently.
Sentimentalising the dead germ, or letting the killed seed stand in for a person's ending, which the group's floor rules out.

Drifting onto a crop the slate carries elsewhere. Gardens of this kind in this district are commonly interplanted, and the film has to stay on the seed and its shade and go nowhere near tapping or any other processing.
Turning the under-fermented beans into a moral about failure, or the good ones into a reward for anybody's care.
Making a smallholding's fermenting shed look like a craft revival or a provenance story, which is the register the whole trade is currently marketed in.

Letting the film's own fascination with what cannot be seen tip into mystery. Nothing about the process is mysterious to the people doing it; they have a hand, a nose and a knife, and they are right often enough to make a living.
drop_if: Fermentation is no longer done on the holding but is taken over by a buyer or a central plant, so the six days cannot be followed in one place.
No household will allow a lot to be followed from the cut to the sacks on its own terms, without the order or the timing being adjusted.
The only gardens reachable are so interplanted with a crop carried elsewhere in this slate that the film cannot stay off it.
The harvest and the filming window cannot be made to meet, so there is no lot to follow.
The film cannot be built without somebody explaining their judgement on camera, which would replace the concept with an interview.
The fermenting is done in a way that has no closed stage at all, so the invisibility the whole film rests on is not there.

connections.note: From a season of several dozen ordered judgements made in the open to six days of ordered change that nobody can look at.
Both are about a change that removes the ground rather than the growth: one inside a closed heap where it cannot be seen, one lifted out of a slope in slabs where it can.
The same far-shore question approached through what carries people across; this one refuses to film a crossing at all and says why.

selection.reason: It is the only construction found for this concept in which the decisive change is genuinely unwatchable, genuinely irreversible and genuinely at the end of a fixed order, so the film can say plainly what it cannot show instead of substituting an image for it.

review.note: Rebuilt 2026-09-24. What was dropped, plainly: the entire crossing. The previous version filmed people crossing a stream by a rope tied to a tree, which was the sources' canal simile taken literally. It is gone for three reasons, any one of which would have been enough. Rope and hand-hauled crossings are a banned archetype in this slate and two other films already carry a crossing. A community's lack of a bridge would have been used to supply the film's drama, which is extractive whatever the narration says. And staging the simile would have produced exactly the reading C100's digest names as the concept's worst: a leap, a threshold, a brave moment. What replaced it: a six-day closed cocoa ferment, in a different province, in which the change that the whole process exists for happens inside each seed, in the dark, at an hour nobody can name, and after which nothing in the rest of the chain can put any of it back. The concepts are unchanged and both links are kept. How C100 is handled without a leap: the process on screen takes six days and four of them look like nothing, so the film's own rhythm refuses the instant; the narration states the source's own order and its seven-place limit rather than dramatising any one moment [C100-P4:L42; C100-P4:L74]; it states that the run arises only after the six worldly purifications are complete [C100-P:L93]; it uses the archer with his face bound in a cloth as its main image, because that image keeps the preparation and removes the sight, where the rope image keeps the drama [C100-P4:L61–L67]; the rope image is spoken once, named as the source's picture, and immediately followed by the film saying that what it is a picture of cannot be filmed at all, since its object is the unconditioned [C100-P4:L44–L46]; the film's only other decisive beat is an audit that counts what is still wrong [C100-P4:L83–L93; C100-P4:L95]; and the closing beat narrates the source's own line that a person who has made this change may afterwards be very heedless [C100-P4:L81], which is the plainest available refusal of the personal-growth reading. Both digests were re-read as a new reader and every citation was re-tested line by line against the source files. Only one citation survives from the previous pass, C100-P4:L44–L46, and its function is completely different: it was the film, and it is now a quotation the film declines to stage. Everything else is new to this pass. C098-P4:L205–L249 has been narrowed from a range to the four individual lines that actually carry suppression, displacement and cutting off, and C098-P4:L145, L143 and L149 have been added so that the irreversibility is stated as the removal of a ground rather than as a victory. A risk has been added about the three piles of cut beans, because a grading test is the one thing in this film that could become a ranking of people, which both digests forbid outright.

suggested_location.name: The mid-country mixed gardens and smallholder fermenting sheds of the Galigamuwa division, in the Kegalle District

also_known_as.name: kokoa
also_known_as.meaning: the crop itself, Theobroma cacao, grown here as an understorey tree in mixed gardens rather than as a plantation

also_known_as.name: pod storage
also_known_as.meaning: the several days for which cut pods are deliberately left in a heap before they are broken, which is a stage of the process and not a delay

also_known_as.name: sweatings
also_known_as.meaning: the liquid that runs out through the floor of the fermenting box in the first days as the sheath around the seed breaks down

also_known_as.name: cut test
also_known_as.meaning: the standard check, made by bisecting a sample of beans lengthwise and reading how far the colour and the internal fissuring have gone; the only way to see the result is to destroy the sample

suggested_location.region: Kegalle District, Sabaragamuwa Province: the mid-country intermediate zone on the steep garden slopes west of the hills, in the small stream valleys away from the main road towns
suggested_location.why_here: Because the crop is documented in this district, the agro-ecological zone is the one the crop is said to do best in, and the scale is domestic rather than industrial. The island's export agriculture department names this district among the six main cocoa-growing districts and gives the national extent as under two thousand hectares in total, which is small enough that the crop is a garden component rather than an industry; the same source describes the crop as grown in fairly dense shade and gives fermentation of five to six days for the common type against one to two for another, followed by washing and sun drying to a low moisture content. The mid-country intermediate zone, which this district sits in, is described as the best zone for both growth and yield. That combination is what the film needs: a real working process, at household scale, in a layered garden that is beautiful from the air before anything is said about it, in a district that holds nothing else this slate is using. The chain is short and in one place — tree, heap, box, leaves, drying floor, sacks — with no auction, no landing and no middle stage in another town. And the constraint is a property of the material and runs one way: the pod has to be caught at a ripeness that is judged and not measured, the seed cannot wait, the six days cannot be paused or re-run, and nothing after them repairs what they did or failed to do. This division is inland, obscure and off the tourist routes, and is deliberately chosen away from the district's better-known towns and away from a division with a recent disaster history that the film has no business bringing in.
what_to_film: The valley and the garden canopy from height in the half hour after first light and again in the last half hour, so the storeys separate and the mist sits in the folds.
The pods low and close under the canopy, in overcast light, growing straight off the trunks and main branches.
The cut: a knife on a pole, the pod coming away, and the pod landing in leaf litter, at arm's length and without a reaction shot.
The heap of cut pods lying in the shade, filmed twice several days apart from exactly the same position, because it is the first stage in which nothing appears to happen.
Pods broken and the wet seed lifted out in its white sheath, close and slow.
The box being filled, the surface levelled by hand, and the banana leaves laid over and pressed down, held long, because it is the last moment at which anything can be changed.
The four closed days as four days: liquid running out under the box, a corner of leaf lifted, a hand going down into the heap and coming back, the leaf replaced. The same framing each time.
The turn: the whole heap forked over, steam, fresh leaves laid on.
The first cut test at arm's length: one bean sliced through its length and the cut face held up to the light.
A hundred beans bisected in a row on a board and counted into piles, filmed from directly above and never intercut with anybody's face.
The drying floor in the hard middle of the day: raking, turning by foot, the bands the rake leaves, and the trays pulled in against rain.
One frame at last light containing the garden, the shed, the empty box and the sacks at once, from height.
suggested_location.access: By road inland from the main highway and then on lanes and farm tracks; the gardens are private smallholdings and the fermenting boxes stand in house compounds and lean-tos, so everything depends on the household whose garden and box these are agreeing, and on approaching through the export agriculture extension service or a growers' group they already deal with rather than cold. The film needs a continuous stay of about ten days rather than visits, because the six closed days are the film, and the timing is set by when a lot is cut. There is no restricted-access problem here; the real difficulties are terrain and weather. The slopes are steep, the tracks are poor and the district is landslide-prone in heavy rain, so the schedule has to be able to lose days. Drying is done in the open and a wet spell puts a lot back. Drone flight over occupied smallholdings and dense canopy needs the household's agreement whatever the general position is, and mist in these valleys closes the elevated views for much of the morning. Gardens in this district are commonly interplanted with crops carried elsewhere in this slate, so the holding has to be one where the film can stay entirely on the seed.
suggested_location.best_time: Inside the harvest, which follows the crop rather than the calendar, and then a dry, still stretch, because the drying is done in the open. About ten days followed straight through: the garden and the cut on the first day, the pod heap across the days it actually lies, the filling of the box, the six closed days as six days, the cut test, and the drying that follows. A second lot is worth planning for, because a lot that comes out badly is part of the subject and cannot be arranged, and because a single rained-on drying floor can cost a whole ending.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only, and unverified on the ground. From the island's own export agriculture department: the total extent of the crop nationally is about eighteen hundred hectares; the main growing districts are six, of which this is one; the crop is grown in fairly dense shade, generally under other tree crops; fermentation takes one to two days for one type and five to six days for the other, by sweat box, heap, tray or box according to scale, cost and labour; and the beans are then washed to remove the sheath and dried in the sun to a moisture content of seven to eight per cent. From general sources on the district: it sits in the mid-country intermediate zone, which is described as the best agro-ecological zone for this crop, and its minor export crops include cocoa alongside coffee, pepper, clove and nutmeg. The detailed practice the film is built on comes from general cocoa post-harvest sources and is not specific to this island or this district: pods cut at a ripeness judged by colour and sound, pods held in a heap for some days before breaking, wet seed heaped in a box lined and covered with banana leaves, the first turn at about forty-eight hours and a second about forty-eight hours later with fresh leaves added each time, the sheath liquefying and draining away through the floor of the box, and the cut test made from the end of the fifth day by bisecting a sample lengthwise and grading it into well, partly and under-fermented. That block of detail is the largest single assumption in this record and is the first thing to check on the ground. Three further things the film depends on are inferences about this district: that fermentation is still done on the holding rather than by a buyer or a central plant, that a whole lot can be followed in one place from the cut to the sacks, and that a holding can be found where the film can stay entirely off the other crops these gardens carry. The coordinates are a published position for the division's centre and are a direction towards the country the film needs, not a survey: no garden, holding, box, group or household has been identified or approached, and no permission has been sought from anybody. No photograph of this district's cocoa gardens, of a smallholder fermenting box or of any part of this work was found on Wikimedia Commons; the one image is of cacao seed in fermentation, photographed elsewhere.

unknowns: Whether fermentation is still done on the holding in this district, or whether wet seed is now sold to a buyer or a central plant, which would remove the film's entire middle.

Whether the practice assumed here — a heap of pods held before breaking, a leaf-lined box, turns at about forty-eight hour intervals, a cut test from the fifth day — actually describes how it is done in these gardens.
Whether a lot large enough to fill a box is produced by one holding, or whether lots are pooled between households, which would change what the film is following.
When the harvest falls for any given garden, and whether it can be made to meet a filming window of about ten continuous days.
Whether a household will allow a lot to be followed from the cut to the sacks without the order or the timing being adjusted, and on whose introduction.
Whether a holding can be found where the film can stay entirely on this crop, given how commonly these gardens are interplanted with crops carried elsewhere in this slate.
Whether height can be obtained over these valleys given the mist and the terrain, and whether the garden's storeys read from the air as strongly as they appear to from the ground.
Whether a closed stage exists at all in the local practice, since the film's whole argument rests on four days in which nothing can be seen.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
